64.0.s.en: (1) The plots of the wicked against the righteous

64.0.0.en: 1- Hear my voice, O God, in my prayer: preserve my life from fear of the enemy.

64.0.1.en: 1- David sensed the plots of the enemies devised against him, so he took refuge in God with a complaint, asking for His help, not only to nullify these plots, but also that He might remove fear from his heart, so that he would not fear the enemies; for God is with him, and no one can overcome him. He also asks that God remove from his heart the fear of the demons, for they are nothing before God's protection of him.

64.0.2.en: 2- This cry to God is a prophecy about Christ on the cross, as He asks the Father to hear His prayer, and this proves the humanity of Christ. This cry is also a prophecy about the cries of the martyrs and of the suffering Church in every generation.

64.1.0.en: 2- Hide me from the secret counsel of the wicked; from the insurrection of the workers of iniquity:

64.1.1.en: 1- David asks God to protect him and cover him, so that the plots of the enemies may not strike him, especially since their numbers are great and they are a multitude larger than he; but his reliance on the power of God reassures him.

64.1.2.en: 2- David also asks, on behalf of every believer, that God cover him from the nakedness of sin and its shame, so that the multitude of demons, who want to make him fall and destroy him, may not gloat over him.

64.1.3.en: 3- The plots of the Jews against Christ were many, and they gathered in a great crowd; so this verse is a prophecy about Christ.

64.2.0.en: 3- Who whet their tongue like a sword, and bend their bows to shoot their arrows, even bitter words:

64.2.1.en: Whet: said of a sword, meaning to make it sharp; it means here that their tongues are strong and sharp in hurting him.

64.2.2.en: Bend: to fix the arrow on the string, ready to hit its target. It means here the strength of their tongues, which direct violent words to strike David.

64.2.3.en: David describes the words of his enemies, and their tongues, as a whetted sword, very sharp, and as an arrow aimed precisely at its target; he also describes their words as bitter, and this shows the extent of David's suffering from the harsh words of his enemies against him.

64.3.0.en: 4- That they may shoot in secret at the perfect: suddenly do they shoot at him, and fear not.

64.3.1.en: 1- David's enemies were lying in wait for him everywhere; even when he hid from their eyes they would go to him and shoot him with their arrows, that is, they never left him in rest, but pursued him everywhere and fell upon him suddenly to destroy him, and they did not fear God, though he was righteous and perfect and had not harmed them in anything; but they are wicked, and their nature is evil, so they do evil even to the righteous.

64.3.2.en: 2- This verse applies, in the spirit of prophecy, to Christ, who hid His divinity and walked in righteousness, but the wicked Jews devised plots against Him and fell upon Him with their words and their embarrassing questions, and even cried for His crucifixion after they attacked Him suddenly in the garden and seized Him, and they did not fear God in all that they did.

64.4.0.en: 5- They encourage themselves in an evil matter: they commune of laying snares privily; they say, Who shall see them?

64.4.1.en: Encourage themselves: they embolden and strengthen themselves.

64.4.3.en: 1- David showed that his enemies were encouraging themselves to wrong him by evil deeds. They would set snares for him, hiding them in the ground and covering them so that they would not appear, in order that David might fall into them. And while they dug these snares they said within themselves that no one sees us, because they did it in secret, forgetting that God sees them and will repay them for their evils.

64.4.4.en: 2- The buried snares are either an ambush to fall upon David and kill him, or evil lusts that entice people with their pleasures, as Satan devised for David the snare of the wife of Uriah the Hittite, so he fell with her, and then repented and turned back.

64.4.5.en: 3- This verse is a prophecy of what happened to Christ, when the Jews agreed to kill Him and tried to ensnare Him with a word, then cried "Crucify Him, crucify Him," and devised a plot to seize Him by means of Judas Iscariot, His disciple, who gave them the sign of the kiss to betray Him. They did all this and forgot that God sees them and will repay them for their deeds; so Jerusalem was destroyed in AD 70 at the hands of the Romans, and a huge number of Jews were killed.

64.5.0.en: 6- They search out iniquities; they accomplish a diligent search: both the inward thought of every one of them, and the heart, is deep.

64.5.1.en: 1- David continues to describe the wicked who are hostile to him, saying that they devise varied evils, and their inventions were precisely planned to entrap David and every righteous man, such as the revolt of Absalom, David's son, against his father, his driving him out and his attempt to kill him; this is an invention that would not occur to anyone's mind, that a son should attack his father and try to destroy him. Likewise Satan made David's friend Ahithophel devise a plan to kill David. So we see the heart of the wicked man is deep, full of evil, and inventions of iniquity.

64.5.2.en: 2- This verse also applies to Christ, for the people whom Christ fed, whose sick He healed and from whom He cast out demons, rose up against Him and demanded, "Crucify Him, crucify Him." Moreover, Satan caused Christ's own disciple Judas Iscariot to rise against Him, to sell Him to the Jews and betray Him to them.

64.5.3.en: Even if the plots and schemes of the wicked are precisely planned and hidden so that the righteous may fall into them, do not be troubled; for everything is naked and open before God, and He is able to uncover these snares and rescue you from them, for He is your God who loves you and cares for you, and you will glorify Him for rescuing you.

64.6.0.en: 7- But God shall shoot at them with an arrow; suddenly shall they be wounded.

64.6.1.en: 1- God was long-suffering toward the wicked, so they devised many plots, including varied evil inventions, and God bore with them to give them an opportunity to repent; but if they persist in evil He takes vengeance on them, and shoots them suddenly with a deadly arrow, as He punished King Herod, whom the people of Sidon called a god, so he became proud and thought he was a god; then God struck him with worms and he died (Acts 12:22).

64.6.2.en: 2- We see this verse in the life of Christ, whom the wicked tried to kill and were indeed able to crucify, and He died on the cross; but by His death He trampled death and saved all who believe in Him, for He lifted from them the debt of sin and gave them new life.

64.7.0.en: 8- And they make their own tongues fall upon themselves: all that look upon them shake the head.

64.7.1.en: Shake the head: to wag the head in contempt and mockery at what one sees.

64.7.2.en: If the wicked speak harsh words against the righteous, God makes their tongues come upon their own heads; that is, their evil words and their attempts to ensnare the righteous, they themselves fall into, as divine vengeance upon them. So everyone who passes by them marvels, and even mocks them, because their evil has come upon them.

64.8.0.en: 9- And all men shall fear, and shall declare the work of God; for they shall wisely consider of his doing.

64.8.2.en: 1- After God punishes the wicked and their shame appears before people, all understand the power of God that supports the righteous, that is, David, and they understand God's providence and His care for His children.

64.8.3.en: 2- This verse appears in Christ, over whom the Jews gloated when He was crucified and died, but they understood God's dispensation when they saw that He had risen from the dead, appeared to His disciples, and then ascended into heaven.

64.9.0.en: 10- The righteous shall be glad in the Lord, and shall trust in him; and all the upright in heart shall glory.

64.9.1.en: 1- In conclusion David declares that the righteous man, that is, David, rejoices in God's work with him, and His protection of him, and how He nullified the plots of the enemies and rescued him from them. He also punished them, in order to confirm David in his faith, and indeed all the righteous; for God established righteousness and showed the vanity of evil.

64.9.2.en: 2- This verse applies to Christ, for He is the righteous One who rejoices in the completion of the mystery of redemption, and all His disciples rejoice in His resurrection and are strengthened, because God protects them.

64.9.3.en: Be confident of your principles and of your adherence to God's commandments, even if the temporary superiority of the wicked appears; but in the end believe that God will reward you with peace on earth and marvelous joy in heaven. Praise to God for His benefits. To the Chief Musician. A Psalm of David. A Song. "Praise waiteth for thee, O God, in Sion" (v. 1) Introduction:

64.9.5.en: 2- When was it written? It is not known precisely, and some think that David wrote it when he brought up the ark of the covenant of God from the house of Obed-edom the Gittite, where it stayed three months (2 Sam 6:13-16).

64.9.6.en: 3- This psalm is liturgical; the children of Israel used to recite it at the feast of firstfruits (Lev 23:9-12), when the fields are clothed with wheat (v. 13). The Church prays its first and second verses on the feasts of the Cross and on Palm Sunday, because through the cross and salvation Christ opened the door for the whole world to believe in Him and praise Him. Likewise in the funeral prayers verse 4 is said, and also on the Feast of Nayrouz verse 11 is prayed.

64.9.7.en: 4- This psalm is considered one of the Messianic psalms, because it is a prophecy about Christ the Savior, who forgives the sins of those who believe in Him (v. 3).

64.9.8.en: 5- This psalm, with the three psalms that follow it, offers praise and thanksgiving to God, and there are the two words

64.9.9.en: 6- This psalm does not occur in the prayers of the Agpeya.

65.0.0.en: 1- Praise waiteth for thee, O God, in Sion: and unto thee shall the vow be performed.

65.0.1.en: 1- David declares that God deserves praise in Zion, where His great temple is, and there vows are paid to God, that is, worship and offerings of love, and the promises made to God are fulfilled; because He is a God able to do all things, and He alone is the Savior of man, and His love and care deserve our thanks and praise.

65.0.2.en: 2- Zion means the high hill on which Jerusalem is built, for praise lifts us up to the heavenly things, so that we live a spirituality that rises above the evil thoughts of the world, and we offer praise in the Church of the New Testament in preparation for offering unceasing praise in the heavenly Jerusalem.

65.0.3.en: 3- The Babylonians tried to make the Jews praise God in Babylon, but they refused, because praise and worship are only in Jerusalem, in the temple of God, that is, in Zion. Perhaps the Jews in captivity used to say this verse: that praise should be in Zion only and not in any other place, since there is only one God whose temple is in Zion.

65.1.0.en: 2- O thou that hearest prayer, unto thee shall all flesh come.

65.1.1.en: 1- Since David and all the believers offered their praises in Zion, God heard and answered them, and this encouraged people in the whole world to believe in God, pray to Him and praise Him. This is a clear prophecy about the faith of the Gentiles; for though the Jews used to reject this, David, as a spiritual man, had the faith of the Gentiles revealed to him by God.

65.1.2.en: 2- God's hearing of prayers shows His love for people, and David's wishes that all people come to God show the breadth of David's heart and his love for the Gentiles; for David's heart was filled with the love of God through the abundance of his prayers.

65.2.0.en: 3- Iniquities prevail against me: as for our transgressions, thou shalt purge them away.

65.2.1.en: David considers that his sins have become heavy upon him, because the burden of sin is the heaviest burden a person suffers. But David hastened to God with repentance and confessed his sins and his suffering from them. At the same time he declared his faith that God alone is able to atone for these sins and forgive them. This is a clear prophecy about Christ the Redeemer, who atones for our sins.

65.3.0.en: 4- Blessed is the man whom thou choosest, and causest to approach unto thee, that he may dwell in thy courts: we shall be satisfied with the goodness of thy house, even of thy holy temple.

65.3.1.en: God's love appears in His offering heavenly glory to whoever believes in Him, prays to Him, praises Him and confesses his sins. The prophet David shows that heavenly glory is given to the chosen, that is, those who have believed in God; God brings them near to Himself on earth, lets them enjoy His blessings through their worship of Him in His temple, and satisfies them with His love. This satisfaction is a symbol of what Christ gives in His Church to those who believe in Him, where He gives them the fruits and gifts of the Holy Spirit and satisfies them with His Holy Mysteries and the means of grace. All that they receive in the Church is also a pledge of what they will enjoy forever in the Kingdom; therefore the Church bids farewell to her departed beloved and recites this verse in the funeral prayer.

65.3.2.en: The great salvation that Christ accomplished for us on the cross, and offers to us in the Church on the altar every day, as true Body and Blood, deserves thanks and praise from you every day. And when you give thanks, your enjoyment of God's blessings and gifts increases at all times.

65.4.0.en: 5- By terrible things in righteousness wilt thou answer us, O God of our salvation; who art the confidence of all the ends of the earth, and of them that are afar off upon the sea:

65.4.1.en: 1- God's fearful justice appeared when the Father offered the greatest gift to the world, giving His only-begotten Son on the cross. This justice was fearful to the demons, whom Christ bound by His cross, and by this justice God answered His children who confessed their sins to Him and granted them His salvation. When the world saw God's fearful justice they feared and believed in Him, because they saw His miracles and His power, for He glorified those who confessed His name and destroyed sinners, such as Ananias and Sapphira (Acts 5:1-11). He is the Savior of His children, like the Apostles whom He strengthened, so that the world feared them despite their personal weakness, and they spread the preaching in the whole world, opening the door of salvation through Christ to everyone who believes in Him.

65.4.2.en: 2- As for God's wonderful salvation and His fearful justice, the Gentiles sensed it, and that there is no God but Him alone, so they believed in Him and trusted in Him, not disturbed by the agitation of the wicked or the changes of life.

65.5.0.en: 6- Which by his strength setteth fast the mountains; being girded with power:

65.5.1.en: Girded: one who ties on a girdle, which is a belt placed around the waist.

65.5.2.en: 1- God's power appears in that He sets fast the mountains, which are the strongest and most firmly rooted things on earth, that is, they are fixed and not shaken. He is also the one who sets fast the moral mountains, meaning His holy children, such as the Apostles, the martyrs and the fathers of monasticism, who stood firm against all the wars of the devil. On the contrary, everyone who relied on his own strength, such as the kings of the earth and the great kingdoms, were all subject to perishing and overthrow.

65.5.3.en: 2- God is able to do all things, and David likens Him to a man who has girded himself with power; for whoever prepares for any work girds his clothes in readiness for the work, but God has complete power over all things, and nothing is too hard for Him, and therefore He is able to save us.

65.5.4.en: 3- If God is the one who sets fast the mountains and is girded with power, then everyone who believes in Him and holds fast to His commandments is firm like the mountain and is girded with the strength of God, so he gains power to do great works and overcomes Satan.

65.6.0.en: 7- Which stilleth the noise of the seas, the noise of their waves, and the tumult of the people.

65.6.1.en: Noise: the loud sound of the dashing waves.

65.6.3.en: 1- God's power appears in stilling the loud sounds resulting from the dashing of the waves, which terrify the passengers of ships because they threaten them with drowning. The seas signify the world, and the noise of their waves is the loud sounds arising from the disturbances and changes of the world; these God stills in the ears of His children, so they are not troubled by them. Likewise the tumult of the people, that is, the pride and agitation of men against the children of God; He intervenes and stills the power of evil and protects His children. God permits the agitation of the world, for this is its nature, but He intervenes to protect His children, so they live in safety and peace in the midst of disturbances, because of His care and power.

65.6.4.en: 2- This is what Christ did when the waves rose and nearly sank the boat in which He was riding with His disciples, and He arose from His sleep and commanded the winds and the waves to be still, and they obeyed Him, all by the authority of His divinity.

65.7.0.en: 8- They also that dwell in the uttermost parts are afraid at thy tokens: thou makest the outgoings of the morning and evening to rejoice.

65.7.1.en: 1- Before the signs of God, such as the ten plagues and the parting of the Red Sea (Ex 7-14), the Gentiles look on and fear the God of Israel, so that some of them believed and joined the people of God, such as Rahab (Josh 6:25). The greatest sign is the Incarnation of Christ and His redemption, as the prophet Isaiah declared (Isa 7:14).

65.7.2.en: 2- All nature rejoices in its Creator and Ruler, and David chooses from it the sun at the outgoing of the morning when it rises, and the time of evening when it sets. The evening signifies the time of the cross and the death and burial of Christ, and the outgoing of the morning signifies His resurrection. The morning and evening also signify the east and the west, that is, the whole world, meaning that Christ by His redemption and resurrection gladdened the whole world, east and west.

65.7.3.en: Contemplate God's power in nature and in the Holy Bible, and you will sense His greatness. This produces in you the fear of Him and the love of Him; fear leads you to repent of your sins, and love leads you to cling to Him and enjoy fellowship with Him through prayers and readings.

65.8.0.en: 9- Thou visitest the earth, and waterest it: thou greatly enrichest it with the river of God, which is full of water: thou preparest them corn, when thou hast so provided for it.

65.8.1.en: 1- God's care for man appears in His concern for the cultivated land that feeds man, as He gives it water from the rivers and springs to water its crops. This water is so abundant that it fills the channels that water the land, so man is not in need and does not go hungry. God's visiting the earth reassures man that his life is in the hand of God, who cares for him. We see in the East great rivers, such as the Nile, the Jordan, the Tigris and the Euphrates, and if the water in these rivers falls short, prayer to God makes Him fill them, as happened in Egypt at the beginning of the nineteenth century, in the days of Muhammad Ali, when Pope Peter El-Gawli prayed. This water signifies the work of the Holy Spirit, who waters the believer, that is, the crop, so that he is firmly planted in the earth, that is, the Church, and lives with God.

65.8.2.en: 2- God's preparing of the earth is not limited to the water of rivers, but He also prepares the earth and waters it with rains, as in the land of Canaan, so God gives His children the early and the latter rain to water the plants, so they eat their food in abundance. In the rains we see the blessings of heaven, which prepare the food of His children, not only material food, but rather spiritual, for He always satisfies them with His love and His fellowship, so they cling to Him and trust in Him.

65.9.0.en: 10- Thou waterest the ridges thereof abundantly: thou settlest the furrows thereof: thou makest it soft with showers: thou blessest the springing thereof.

65.9.1.en: Ridges: plural of the furrow, which is the cut of the plow in the earth in which the seeds are placed.

65.9.2.en: Furrows: plural of the trench, which is an elongated cut in the earth, and the farmer needs to level it so that he can sow the land.

65.9.4.en: Springing: its crops, such as wheat and barley ...

65.9.5.en: 1- In His concern for man's food, God cares for the cultivated land, so He prepares the earth and makes it level, and it is rid of its trenches and becomes fit for sowing. When the plow cuts it and makes furrows in it, and the farmer puts the seed in it, God waters it with rains and softens the clods of earth, that is, breaks them up, so the crops grow in it and give their yield abundantly by the blessing of God, to satisfy man's bodily needs.

65.9.6.en: 2- So also God cares for the soul: He prepares it, that is, removes from it the results of sins and makes it level; He softens it, that is, examines it through repentance and examination of the soul, then waters it with the waters of the Holy Spirit and nourishes it with His Body and Blood, so it grows spiritually and bears fruit, and He blesses these spiritual fruits.

65.10.0.en: 11- Thou crownest the year with thy goodness; and thy paths drop fatness.

65.10.1.en: 1- So we see God's goodness and mercies blessing the whole year with all the crops sown in it, whether winter or summer. The earth is filled with the greenery on which the animals feed, and the effects of the blessing of the cultivated land appear in animals that give milk and meat full of fatness.

65.10.2.en: 2- God also speaks to the spiritual man with His mercies and goodness throughout the year, that is, throughout his life, and keeps him, causes him to grow and blesses him; likewise the effects of His care for him appear, for He gives him grace in the eyes of those around him, and he becomes an example to others, and so influences them. Thus the fatness of the work of grace in him appears.

65.11.0.en: 12- They drop upon the pastures of the wilderness: and the little hills rejoice on every side.

65.11.3.en: 1- When God blesses the earth He cares for all its kinds: the plains, or the valleys in the wilderness, He gives crops that the animals eat, so they become pastures, and when these animals are satisfied they give fatness of meat and milk. Likewise the hills are filled with pastures and the animals feed on them, so that all are in gladness and joy.

65.11.4.en: 2- The plains of the wilderness signify the humble and all believers, while the hills signify those advanced spiritually, who are raised toward heaven, that is, all believers rejoice. The wilderness also signifies the Gentiles, who were barren and were filled with greenery by the grace of God, and the hills signify the Jews who knew God and rose to Him from the days of the fathers, who rejoiced and were glad when they believed in Christ.

65.12.0.en: 13- The pastures are clothed with flocks; the valleys also are covered over with corn; they shout for joy, they also sing.

65.12.1.en: Covered over: wearing a cloak (a coat), that is, clothed.

65.12.3.en: 1- The prophet David continues to describe the blessings of God, who shepherds His people, so He blesses His land and makes the meadows fill and be clothed with flocks, and the valleys likewise are covered with wheat. Man and animal eat, and therefore all shout for joy, because they are satisfied and give thanks to God.

65.12.4.en: 2- The flocks signify those advanced spiritually, and the valleys signify the beginners; all are clothed and satisfied and give thanks to God, praising and glorifying Him in joy.

65.12.5.en: If only you would thank God every day for His gifts and His blessings to you, spiritual and material, then your heart will be at peace and rejoice, and God's gifts to you will even increase, so you become a light to the world, calling them without speaking to life with God, as they see in your life calm, peace and happiness.

65.12.6.en: All praise God. To the Chief Musician. A Song. A Psalm. "Make a joyful noise unto God, all the earth" (v. 1) Introduction:

65.12.7.en: 1- The name of the author of the psalm is not mentioned, so it is counted among the orphan psalms, whose author is unknown; it may be that David wrote it, or someone else.

65.12.8.en: 2- This psalm is liturgical; it offers praise to God and calls the Gentiles to praise Him.

65.12.9.en: 3- This psalm is a prophecy about what happened in the days of King Hezekiah, at the defeat of Assyria before him, and about the victory of the Maccabees over the Greeks, and their praising God.

65.12.10.en: 4- This psalm is a clear prophecy about the faith of the Gentiles in Christ, and the praise of Him by the whole earth, Jews and Gentiles.

65.12.11.en: 5- This psalm also carries a prophecy about the resurrection of Christ, the Giver of life (v. 9), and in the title of this psalm in the Septuagint translation there is the phrase "for the resurrection."

65.12.12.en: 6- This psalm does not occur in the prayers of the Agpeya.
